summary: Department-scoped Slack prefix enforcer and Confluence space retirement wizard
description:
Issue summary: We want an automated, department-scoped policy implementation that enforces Slack channel name prefixes and synchronizes channel topic tags to Confluence space metadata. In addition, add a Confluence Space Retirement Wizard that identifies stale spaces, notifies owners, and opens templated Jira tasks for archival.

Impact: Inconsistent channel naming and stale Confluence spaces cause discovery problems, oncall confusion, and compliance risk for data retention audits. Owners currently rely on manual processes which are error-prone and time-consuming.

Request: Build two related automations: (1) Slack Prefix Enforcer: a bot or Slack app that ensures new public/private channel names follow a department prefix pattern (e.g., eng-, data-, infra-, biz-). When a channel is created without a valid prefix, the bot should suggest a corrected name, optionally rename where permitted, and add topic tags matching department metadata. The enforcer must support SCIM and workspace admin constraints and have an admin bypass list. (2) Confluence Space Retirement Wizard: scheduled job that flags spaces with no page updates in 12 months, emails space owners with a review link, offers one-click archive or extend actions, and can create a Jira task using a template if the owner requests archival work.

Background/context: This ties into the Channel Naming Standards and Space Lifecycle Runbook maintained by Ops. Similar efforts referenced: INT-31456 (ephemeral channel lifecycle automation) and INT-42351 (templated runbook provisioning). We need a lean implementation that minimizes permissions escalation and keeps audit trails.

Proposed implementation steps: 1) Design policy schema (yaml/json) for prefix rules and department mappings. 2) Prototype Slack app using existing slack-bots repo and SCIM APIs to validate creation events and apply topic tags. 3) Hook Slack actions to create an audit Jira ticket when renames or bypasses occur. 4) Implement Confluence scheduled service using REST API to compute staleness, send templated notifications, and create Jira tasks for archival. 5) Add Admin UI in Ops Console (or a minimal Confluence macro) for owners to perform archive/extend. 6) Add observability: metrics for enforcement hits, renames, bypasses, space retirement emails, and tasks created.

Acceptance criteria: - New Slack channels are validated on creation; >95% of non-compliant creations receive a corrective suggestion within 30s. - Admin bypass list works and is auditable in Jira. - Confluence retirement job identifies stale spaces and triggers emails; owners can archive or extend through the provided workflow. - Auditable Jira tasks are created for archival actions and linked back to the Confluence space. - Implementation documented and a runbook created in Confluence.

Security/permissions note: Plan must avoid broad impersonation tokens. Prefer granular bot tokens and workspace admin scopes only where required. Obtain security sign-off prior to production rollout.
investigation_notes:
Checked current slack-bots repo for similar functionality; found a rename helper but no enforcement hook. Verified Confluence REST endpoints allow querying last-modified; we need to validate paging for large tenant. Slack SCIM may require SCIM admin role — confirm with Identity team. Hypothesis: We can implement soft-enforcement (suggest + rename when permitted) to reduce friction on rollout.

Preliminary checks performed: - Confirmed channel creation events available via Events API. - Ran a small script to list spaces and compute last-updated dates (sample run on 2026-03-05). - Identified potential rate limits for Confluence calls; will add exponential backoff.
